utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-95-5/18-PT, The Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, I take it, as always, that you appear and represent yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take my headphones off?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm looking for Serbian channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Number 4. No sorry, no sorry. My mistake. Is it 5? 6. I'll start again, then. You represent yourself as before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, and that will be the case until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. This date for this Status Conference was chosen in the hope that it would be shortly after the question of the amendment to the indictment had been resolved, and it looked as though that was how things had worked out, until earlier this week, when the Prosecution made a motion for re-consideration of the Chamber's decision to amend the First Amended Indictment, and that's the subject that I want to deal with, first of all, in the course of this Status Conference. And I'm going to ask the Prosecution for certain information. But, first of all, I'll take from the Prosecution the appearances. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alan Tieger, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and case manager Iain Reid for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you explain what has happened in relation to the decision to amend the indictment and the motion that you made subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The motion, as I believe the Court is aware, focuses on one aspect of the schedule, that is, annex B, and scheduled incident 18.2. This incident was specified in the schedule as our motion indicated that there was material to support the inclusion of that incident and, as a result of an administrative error, in instead of the supporting material references to the proper page numbers, the supporting material for scheduled incident 18.1 was included twice. In short, the same -- the wrong references to the same witness in the same proceeding. And, of course, I hope the motion indicates that the Prosecution acknowledges and regrets the error. Our motion also indicates, however, that it is in the interest of justice for the Court to receive the actual supporting materials and to order the restoration of scheduled incident 18.2 of annex (B) to the indictment. We've indicated, as I believe, that this is an important incident. There are significant number of victims. There is the approximate presence of the accused. The Rules themselves, that is 47(f), provide for the subsequent provision of omitted materials that support either specific charges or scheduled incidents. When that can be easily remedied, it will not cause any prejudicial delay in the proceedings because of the stage of the proceedings and because the Rule 72 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These are -- and if I can just stop you there. It may or may not be appropriate to go into these additional issues. I just wanted clarification of what the problem was so that everyone is clear here what we are dealing with. Now, Mr. Tieger, the decision that the Trial Chamber made found that there was no supporting material for three incidents. Your motion is related to one particular incident. It's quite clear to me what that relates to. Are you saying that have you no intention of raising either of the other two?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We didn't raise it at the time, Your Honour, because of our concern over this incident. In particular, that is not to say that -- I mean, I think the nature of the problem with respect to the other two incidents -- well, specifically with respect to the incident, the number of which I don't recall, but in Krupa, could be just as easily remedied as the Court is aware. It's a discrepancy between the date and supporting materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this the Petar Kocic elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is a mistake a -- inconsistency between the materials supporting the charge and the terms of the charge. The supporting material refers to August, and the charge refers to May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. And, Your Honour, that was not intended to be a reference to -- a reference to two incidents, that is, one in the supporting materials and one in the schedule. It was instead a discrepancy between the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. But it's basic. They either have to meet or one doesn't support the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right. But your motion, therefore, is confined to the one that you consider most important?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, this, a situation, gives rise to a motion, which the Chamber has to consider. It has no option. The motion is to re-consider the decision to amend the indictment and to allow the Prosecution to add this one further incident, one of the three that we excluded. We were also to stay the effect of our previous decision. We refused to do that so that the indictment was presented as you know on Wednesday. That doesn't, though, prevent the Prosecution from going ahead with this motion. I can't tell them that this is something that's incompetent. It is open to them to make the application, and in the ordinary course there is a period for you to respond. Now in relation to all the other amendments, you responded on points of principle and on points related to the expeditious and fair conduct of the trial. You did not take issue with the detail of the proposed amendment. The -- so what I'd like it know, first of all, is whether have you any particular point that you think you will wish to make about the incident, and including this incident, in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to point out that even the Prosecutor with the vast resources it has at its disposal, and far greater advantage in that respect with respect to my resources and the instruments and vehicles that can I use, did not succeed to this day to get through everything they wanted to. And over the past two or three days, I have received an enormous amount of papers and documents which I found it hard to leaf through. Some of them are just translations which I just received. And as for the indictment, I still do not know whether it is in force or not and whether I'm going to be asked to plead today or not, according to the indictment. Now the Prosecution is criticizing for me not being precise enough on the 6th of August when I had not a single advisor with respect to the Holbrooke Agreement; although, they know full well and exactly what I had in mind when I referred to that, and now they're asking me to give way to them, to show a little leeway with respect to the mistakes and omissions they made. Of course, that is far from what I intend to do. As for the indictment itself it will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, the Prosecution are not asking you for leeway, they're asking the Bench for leeway, and you have the right to take your stand on this. And I just want to be clear, first of all, whether you do take the stand that you wish to resist this change to the indictment because if that is a live issue, then you will not be asked to plead to the indictment today. The Chamber will, first of all, have to decide what to do about this motion. If, on the other hand, you do not consider that you have any other particular points to make, then we can obviously proceed more expeditiously. It's as simple as that. But if you want to respond to this motion to re-consider, and you have points that you want to make in relation to it, then I have to decide what time you ought to have to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I thought that I was expected to do something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. I'm just trying to see if there is an issue here that needs to be explored. I mean, for example you're -- in terms of the rules, the normal process is that you would have 14 days in which to respond to this motion for re-consideration, in light of -- following upon the translation of -- of the motion. However, before deciding whether that's the right course to follow, I would like to know, first of all, whether you do wish to oppose it, and, secondly in broad terms, on what ground you wish to oppose it, and then I will consider what period of time is necessary. It may be that 14 days is quite unnecessary in all the circumstances, particularly in view of the line you have taken so far in relation to the indictment, which I understand and fully appreciate and the Trial Chamber appreciates.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is too much of a major issue for me to state my views without consulting my legal advisors. And they're only around three days a month to visit me. So before I state my views I have to consult them, and I'm sure that we'll avail ourselves of all the rights to object and to respond to the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you see, that's very unhelpful because you are counsel in your case, and the Chamber, when it comes into one of these hearings, expects to be assisted by counsel. Now, what you're say is that you're trying to conduct this case but you're incapable of conducting, and that's an unsatisfactory situation for the Court to be in. I expect you when you come here to have a position on the various issues that have to be addressed by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried that tell you yesterday and today I received a whole pile of papers that I haven't even managed to leaf through, so even if I to have counsel, during a short period of time, I would not be able to state my views in the matter. And regardless of the fact that I represent myself, I have to consult my advisors. I have to have advisors and consult them. And even if I were a lawyer, I would have to do the same. So that's completely regular. It's within my rights. It's within my rights to respond and within these prescribed deadlines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, what you may be claiming is a right to pretend to represent yourself, and we want to be sure that that's not what's happening here, that you are actually representing yourself. I have got to be satisfied that you're capable of doing this job, and it's not sounding that way just at this minute. This is a very minor matter in the overall scheme of this case, and it's very surprising that you are incapable of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I'll answer you. I am capable of dealing with it, and I'll use all my rights to respond to the question. Does that sound clearer to you now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the response to the question is: Do you seek to answer to this motion to amend the indictment further?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karadzic, while this was -- this allegation is one of a grave nature, what we are dealing with here procedurally is fairly minor in the overall context of the process so far and, in particular, in the overall context of the motion to amend the indictment. And it is in my opinion that to allow you until Wednesday of next week to respond to this motion would be perfectly adequate. And, therefore, the order is that the time to respond to the motion will be restricted so that the response will be required on Wednesday of next week, which is the 25th of February.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to express my dissatisfaction with the fact that this deadline has been shortened to such a major question, not only because I am limited and restricted in all other aspects. I don't have a team set up, my resources are nil, and even if they were fully replenished, I could not respond within the deadline prescribed. And as far as I'm concerned, every question is a serious question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now it follows from that decision that I will not be requiring you to plead to the indictment which is there, pending re-consideration of the decision to allow the Prosecution to amend the indictment. The Further Appearance, at which the plea will be tendered, will be adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll indicate to you before we finish this afternoon when the Further Appearance is likely to be. It will be impossible, because of the other commitments of the Tribunal, to state a specific time and date in the course of this hearing. All I can do will be to give you an indication. I want to turn now to the question of disclosure. Now on that subject, Mr. Tieger, who do I address? Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, you have compiled a report dated the 13th of February which indicates the numbers of documents disclosed, and part of that disclosure is in terms of Rule 66(A)(ii) which is a rule that deals with statements of witnesses that you intend to lead at the trial. The document also indicates that what's been disclosed are mainly expert reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's expert reports and experts's testimony, statements, everything related to 23 experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it's restricted to experts, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And now we are actually proceeding now to disclose materials related to international witnesses, because we have actually a schedule for our disclosure internally, and we start with those witnesses where the amount of disclosure is the most complex. And that's the expert and the international witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is 23 experts the sum total of the anticipated experts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is it yet another expert we couldn't disclose yet because of clearance for Rule 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So, in the end, the maximum number of experts likely to be called is 24?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 24, or 25, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you consider that the disclosure of these reports has had any impact in triggering the application of Rule 94 bis?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will definitely file motions to this effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So -- is your answer no? You're saying it doesn't have that effect until you take some other action. Is that your position. The Rule 98 bis says: @the full statement under report of any expert witness shall be disclosed within the time limit described by the Trial Chamber or by the Pre-Trial Judge."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the then -- that disclosure triggers a 30-day period for a response.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is it your submission that the 30 days is running, or do you say that something needs to be done in terms of Rule 94 to start it running.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: According to the Rule, it should actually be left to disclose these -- these materials. However, we have not, in the disclosure letter to the accused, we have not mentioned this rule, so I would think it perhaps a bit unfair now to just say, It's running and you don't know about it. So I think we -- we actually had intended to file a motions to this effect, but we can also, of course, write specific letters to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you'll agree with me that something else, whatever it is, should be done to trigger the effect of Rule 94 bis?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Has the disclosure of these various reports been in both English and B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Not completely, Your Honour. We are still working on certain transcripts. We have disclosed for -- we have disclosed some transcripts in B/C/S but not all, because we don't have them available at the moment. We have a team of 15 people working on the transcribing project, but it's just very time-consuming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you able to identify a number that have been fully disclosed in both languages?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Reid is looking for this, and we'll get to the answer soon. But to my knowledge, no. I think there's still -- there are still even for those where we are very much advanced, there is some issue outstanding. For instance, just to give an example, we have disclosed everything for Mr. Theunens, who is a military expert in intend to call, and we still have not completed his testimony transcription in B/C/S for the for the Gotovina case. So, for him, it's one item outstanding. For the others, it's probably even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in light of the discussion earlier, it's possible - and I'll clarify this before we finish - but it's possible that there be another Status Conference within the next two weeks, roughly two weeks from now, subject to other checks that are being made at the moment. It's clear that the position is not clear enough. It's too confused at the moment in relation to these reports for an order to be made. But you can take it that it will be the aim of the Court to make an order about expert reports the next time there is a Status Conference, so you should bear that in mind in making the arrangements that you are making.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the document which you would get and which I first saw last week, at the end of last week, in fact the beginning of this week, when I saw it, about the number of documents which have been disclosed to you, indicated certain figures about statements of witnesses. It was not clear to me until just now that these are all expert witness statements. It is arguable that the very disclosure of these to you could have had an impact on the time available to you to respond, but the Prosecution position, with which I agree, is that the simple fact of giving you that material does not start any period of time running, and the period for you to react to these, in terms of Rule 94 bis, will not start running until the Court makes an order and no order is going to be made on that today. However, it is possible that an order might be made the next time the Court meets. That can only be decided in the light of the state of documents at that stage, the state of translation, and the extent to which the disclosure has been completed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I appreciate that. Thank you. But it was only today that I saw this. I have this list of some 105.000 pages. Quite a few of these disclosed pages are only referred to in terms of their numbers in the EDS system. At this point, I cannot use it: First of all, because my Defence team hasn't been completed yet; and, secondly, as I've given up on asking for documents on paper, and since I agreed to receive documents in electronic form, it would be good if I were to receive it on CDs or DVDs. I have filed a motion to that effect, because, really, I have so many obstacles in terms of preparing my Defence, that I needed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The document I have, which perhaps has been updated since as a result of inquiry, indicates a larger number of pages than you have just given. I think where I see the figure 105.000 comes from, but I think the Prosecution would claim to have disclosed something in the order of 220.000 pages to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never received that paper. However, what I referred to was what was disclosed until the 10th of December. 105.000 pages. Actually, I am now going to find the name of your associate - I'm sure that you know who I'm talking about - this lady who -- Yvonne Featherstone. She intervened yesterday. She intervened yesterday and that's how I received all this information today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that was on my instructions, Mr. Karadzic, and she is one of the staff who sit in front of me here. Now, there are two matters you've raised, one of which is quite easy to deal with; the other I need to ask some questions of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Featherstone has just clarified for me that the document I'm referring to is one that you have not, in fact, seen. So I'll make sure it's sent to you, but it's a summary giving the total of documents and pages disclosed to you. But let me ask the position about documents simply being disclosed by number. Is this the problem that's already been raised in one of the motions?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's in the motion. Mr. Karadzic has asked for everything disclosed on DVDs or CDs, and we, actually, at the moment are only disclosing Rule 66(A) material and 65 ter material on DVD and CD, while we disclosed the Rule 68 material via the EDS in a very particular Rule 68 folder. And we have explained in our response why we do it this way, and why it would actually be much more practical for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Chamber has your motion on this point in writing, Mr. Karadzic, and we now have a response from the Prosecution, and we will deal with this quickly, and you will get a response to it that explains the position. Now, you'll have an opportunity, as I say, fairly soon in court again to raise issues that may emerge as the result of our decisions on your written motions. I'm much keener to deal with things orally in exchange with you than in writing, which, first of all, causes delay, but, secondly, often causes misunderstanding, and sometimes things are much better explained in court. So we'll leave it until the decision is made on the points you've raised with us, and give you an opportunity to comment when we're in court the next time. I want to go back briefly to the question of the amendment to the indictment, and I want to mention something to you. Your principle motion responding to the motion to amend the indictment was to ask the Trial Chamber to deal with the motion in a way that would identify a part of the case against you to go to trial so that everybody could concentrate on that one part. As you know, the Trial Chamber did not follow that course, and it didn't follow the course because it took the view that it's not open, it's not competent at this stage to do that. But we have mentioned to you the possibility of raising this issue in a preliminary motion once the indictment is finally resolved and you tender your plea again, you may seek to address the provisions of Rule 72(A)(iii), which provides that in a preliminary motion you can seek the severance of counts joined in one indictment. I'm expressing no view on the outcome of any such application. I'm expressing no view on the powers of the Tribunal under that Rule. I'm simply drawing your attention to wording which could be seen to give you an argument for separating part of the indictment for trial. And if you decide to follow that route when you present any preliminary motion, I want to make it clear to you now that the Trial Chamber will be greatly assisted by you identifying clearly how the indictment might be separated with a view to doing that. In other words, how counts of the indictment or charges in the indictment might be separated from others with a view to a trial proceeding but not on the whole indictment. Now, please do not misunderstand this as an indication that that's going to happen. But since you have raised it and made it such an important point of your submission, it's only right that the Trial Chamber should make it clear to you that there does appear at this stage to be a way in which you can at least address the issue and invite the Trial Chamber to consider your position when it was not possible prior to finalising the indictment. I think this next -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have -- or, rather, I have raised question of challenging jurisdiction and amending the indictment, and the preliminary motions, and there are going to be at least ten of them referring to different grounds. If we look at it this way, we see that this is going to be a huge trial that goes beyond the resources that the OTP has, let alone I. Now that I've been here for almost six months, I've been acting in good faith in order to create a process, a trial, that is going to be important for us, the peoples back there, and also for international justice and international law. I believe that many other countries would seeing how the president of a state can be tried. Indeed, as you have seen, there have been no delays on my account. I have been doing everything with full propriety. However, as I look at the indictment I see that this is going to be a gigantic trial. And -- anyway, this is going to be mentioned in all my motions, so you will see what I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The point doesn't get any better for unnecessary repetition, but thank you again for clarifying your position on this. I want now to raise a procedure of which I think will assist everyone involved in this case, and that is amplifying the Prosecution approach to the trial at the earliest possible opportunity. Once the indictment is resolved and we are into the serious stage of exchanging -- or intimating lists of witnesses and exhibits which are actually going to be used in the case, Rule 65 ter (E) will come into play, and the Prosecution will have to provide a pre-trial brief. That Rule, however, envisages the provision of -- the possible provision of a -- an earlier pre-trial brief, and in this case, it's my opinion that the progress of the trial will be greatly assisted by further amplification of the Prosecution case. So I have in mind, Mr. Tieger, to require the Prosecution to provide an interim pre-trial brief, which will -- apart from assisting the accused by identifying the line that's going to be followed at the trial, will assist the Chamber in marshalling the material, the large amount of material, which we anticipate we will have to come to terms with over the next few weeks. Now, can I invite your comments on the sort of time-scale that might be necessary to produce that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you can imagine, we were -- we are working on the pre-trial brief, on the witness list, and of the exhibits -- on the exhibits list, and we have actually internal deadlines for doing this, and we had actually anticipated to file our pre-trial brief and the other 65 ter submissions in April, and that's what we could manage. And I personally, at the moment, cannot see how an interim pre-trial brief could expedite this. But, of course, I hadn't thought of this before, so I'm -- I haven't thought that through. But that was actually our internal schedule, to have everything filed in April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now one of the problems for the Trial Chamber in working out the likely time-scale has been the requirement that no order about a pre-trial brief in its final form can be made until the preliminary motions have been disposed of. And, of course, we're not even at the stage where the time for a preliminary motion is running, and that's largely because of the way the case has been prosecuted so far, as you know. So it's important that the ultimate provision of this should not be delayed to the point where it disables the Trial Chamber from taking steps which it's in a position to take, to familiarise itself with the case as fully as possible. Now, it seems to me that over the next six weeks or so, the person who is going to be most occupied with the preparation of material for the Court's attention will be the accused, who will then be faced with the issue of preliminary motions and any other issues that he intended to raise, and that it's not unreasonable for the Court to ask the Prosecution to use that time to give it a pre-trial brief on an interim basis. Now, the time-scale I have in mind is not much different from yours. I think yours is unrealistic in the context of the Rules as the final date for the pre-trial brief. On the other hand, I don't think it's far off the mark in identifying when it would be reasonable to ask you to outline your case in more detail. So what I shall do is require you to file an interim pre-trial brief on or before the 30th of March. This shouldn't be regarded as something that just has to be done in some form or other to satisfy the strict terms of an order of the Court. In view of the importance of this case, the Trial Chamber would expect that by that date you would be in a position to outline, in terms fairly close to the final terms, the case that you intend to present. Mr. Karadzic seems to have lost track of a time a little. In his comments earlier, he has been here a bit longer than six months already, and that we must never lose sight of.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one question for clarification. Does that mean an interim pre-trial brief including a witness list and exhibits list, or just the pre-trial brief?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is only the pre-trial brief, but my understanding that your pre-trial brief would normally be heavily referenced and footnoted to the witnesses, but a final -- so if it's convenient to you, it would obviously be helpful to the Trial Chamber to have the lists as well. But the lists are not what I'm after. I'm after the outline of the case with reference to the supporting material, and it's that document that will assist us. But if you wish to provide the additional assistance, that's fine. I think it's -- it could be said to become duplication, otherwise, unnecessary, and I don't insist on that, whereas the work of the brief is something that I don't expect to be duplication. I expect that once it's done it will be a question of refinement for the final version.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One other issue, then, that I have to raise with you, Mr. Karadzic, but it's really for information. You have a motion outstanding for the interview of a potential witness on the question of immunity, and you seek the interview -- you seek authority for you, yourself, to carry out that interview. Do you have any information about the availability of the witness should a decision be made to allow that to happen? In other words, can the interview be arranged at short notice, or are you not in a position to tell me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am in a position to clarify that. First of all, I'd like to thank you for bringing it up, but I'd like to ask you that I not be provided with material that have nothing to do with me. I have material that relates to Kosovo. I had to have them translated because they might be relevant but they do not have relevance. Now, I'm trying to resolve all these problems without the Trial Chamber, but in future I'll have to send in my motions to the Trial Chamber in order to be able to defend myself from useless material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me -- you're obviously on to a different subject. Can we come back to Kosovo. Can you deal with the witness, first of all, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There are two problems in that regard. The basic problem is this: The authorities in Serbia have proclaimed statements by seven witnesses which they took with respect to the circumstances. They proclaimed it a state secret. So now it's a problem for me to call those witnesses, to interview them, because most probably they don't dare give a statement because Serbia has proclaimed the whole matter to be a state secret, and I am convinced that those statements are highly important otherwise they wouldn't have been proclaimed a state secret. And I will insist that Serbia lifts this state secrecy, as it has done pursuant to requests from the Prosecution, to do that from the statements, too. The second question is this: For me to be allowed to have the witness come in. He was the foreign minister, Republika Srpska. He's not anybody, and he knows firsthand what was agreed during the negotiations. So I would like to interview him. All the more so, as I don't have the entire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're not really addressing my question. My question is: Do you know whether there are any particular problems about his attendance at the Tribunal. Now, are you saying, first of all, that his prior statement has been declared a state secret?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been informed via Serbia that all seven witness who were interviewed, that their statements have been proclaimed state secrets, and I insist that Serbia lift that ban for publicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are you saying that they would have some control over his attendance here or, alternatively, control over what he could say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They cannot control what he might say, but I'm wondering whether I'm not going to subject him to any dangers in disclosing state secrets. So I don't -- though, I don't think so because he was foreign minister of Republika Srpska, not Serbia. And the second problem is for him to be issued a visa and for his expenses to be paid and travel expenses, as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's a decision, as you know, that we indicated we would postpone until the outcome of the appeal which you have taken against the previous disclosure decision made by this Trial Chamber. I will convey that additional information to the other Judges on the Trial Chamber, and if we have a different view or require more information from you, we will contact you for that. If you hear nothing from us, it will be because we still intend to postpone the decision until the Appeals Chamber has ruled on your appeal. Mr. Tieger, are there any issues that you wish to raise with the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, just one point of clarification, perhaps, Your Honour. The Court inquired about 94 bis and whether or not the disclosure of the expert, previous experts' statements, was intended to trigger or was regarded as triggering 94 bis. I think it's important to clarify that many of those statements basically fell under 66(A)(ii) as prior statements, some of which are not that pertinent to these proceedings, and many of which were not intended to be the statement -- the operative statements which will be relied upon in this proceeding. Numbers of experts are indeed updating their reports with any recently received materials, and I think that's what Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff was alluding to when she suggested that we would be filing something contemporaneously both for notice purposes and for clarification purposes. But, mainly, I didn't want the Court to misunderstand on the basis of what we had suggested that all of those reports were intended to be operative in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it important, though, Mr. Tieger, that expert reports are finalised at a fairly early stage. The Rules are very flexible with expert reports compared with the provisions about other material, and the Trial Chamber had a discussion about this and take the view that we should try to have these in the final form as soon as possible. I think I have formed him -- a wrong impression from the earlier discussion that matters were further advanced than have you indicated, and obviously we would not wish to make an order that would result in a failure or cause you to be unable to organise the material in its most up to date and articulate and comprehensive form. So we would encourage that that these things should be updated and compiled into the most easily read form of all. But I think you should give a degree of priority to this, because it is something that we can get on with while we're prevented from making progress in other fields. So I hope that when we meet again there will be a number of these that with actually be disclosed in terms of Rule 94 bis. It doesn't necessarily need to be them all, but it makes for progress if we get some of them dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, is there any other matter that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd like, first of all, to express my desire that the services of this Tribunal are encouraged to help me so that my Defence team can be completed as soon as possible, because I cannot put up an effective Defence - not because I'm representing myself - but because my Defence team hasn't been completed yet and because it is treated as some auxiliary staff. And when they need to be nominated and appointed, they are treated in one way, and look at conflict of interests and things like that. And when they have to pay them, then they pay them as some auxiliary staff. So I don't think that even a smaller trial than this could be prepared under those conditions. And, secondly, I'd like very kindly to request that you re-consider your decision with respect to the deadline for the motions and submissions. I'm handicapped sufficiently as to time and resources as it is, so I would be very happy if you were to extend the deadlines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the only motion that has been subject of a deadline today is the motion by the Prosecution for re-consideration of the decision on the indictment. And bearing in mind the way you approached the -- approached the issue previously and bearing in mind what you said today, then it seems to me that I have allowed you adequate time to make your submission. If you have a particular submission to make that requires additional time, then, no doubt, you will put that to the Tribunal in writing, but have you not done that in the course of this hearing today. As far as your legal team is concerned, that is a matter between you and the Registry of the Tribunal. You've already raised with the Trial Chamber a fair trial issue, and when there are fair trial issues then it is for the Trial Chamber to intervene. Now, we refuse to intervene because we took the view that the Registry had acted properly in dealing with it. I'm -- I hear what you say about the legal team, but I also know from the terms of the documents that are passing through my hands that you have a large number of people assisting. I understand that the vast majority of these may be acting pro bono, that's a matter for you and them. But the organisation of your team is not a matter that I can attend to here or have any interest in dealing with, or any right -- by interest, I mean any right to deal with. It's a matter for the Registrar unless an issue arises that affects the fairness of the trial. So I can only encourage you to take urgent steps that you see outstanding in that regard express my dismay that it's taking you so long to deal with it. You know what the facilities are and what your entitlement is. It's a management exercise on your part to get them organised into suitable sections to deal with the various parts of your case that you feel they can assist you with. The Trial Chamber is entirety satisfied that for a self-represented accused you have adequate support, and we're also equally satisfied that if you were to apply for full legal aid for the conduct of the trial, that you would be much better supported than you are to deal with the complex issues that will face you in the trial, and you would also be able to play a part in the conduct of your own case as long as that met with the approval of the legal advisors that would then instruct it. So all of that convinces the Trial Chamber that there are no issues affecting the fairness of your trial that currently arise in relation to how your team is composed. Now, I've had a look at the dates that could be available for the next Status Conference. The position is not at all clear because the Tribunal is working at full capacity, and courtroom space is at a premium. I will need to consider further whether adjustments can be made and the timetable affecting other cases to enable us to sit again fairly soon, and a Scheduling Order giving a date will be issued hopefully by Monday. Meanwhile, this Status Conference is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
